summary.headline: Bosch Ltd to acquire related-party Bosch Chassis Systems India (RBIC) for INR9,068.7 crore, ~10.6x FY25 EV/EBITDA, targeted close by end-Q1 FY27.
summary.overview: This transcript covers two investor calls on April 13, 2026, about the proposed acquisition of Bosch Chassis Systems India Pvt Ltd (RBIC), a group company, not a quarterly results call; management said it was in silent period and would not discuss quarterly results. RBIC posted FY25 revenue of about INR4,000 crore and a 19.3% EBITDA margin, with 9M FY26 revenue of about INR3,500 crore. Pro forma FY25 revenue for Bosch Ltd rises about 22% to INR22,000 crore and EBITDA margin improves from 12.8% to 13.9%, with about 5% pro forma EPS accretion. The deal is almost all cash, funded from existing funds and internal accruals, with a small preferential allotment to Robert Bosch Netherlands and Robert Bosch US, and shareholder voting runs April 9 to May 8, 2026.

financial_highlights.metric: Bosch Ltd pro forma FY25 revenue
Pro forma FY25 EBITDA margin (Bosch Ltd)

segments.name: RBIC (Bosch Chassis Systems India) - safety and braking
segments.commentary: Covers ABS, ESP, occupant safety sensors and controllers, EV new braking systems (iBooster, integrated power brakes) and conventional actuation; about one-third two-wheeler and the rest passenger and commercial vehicles per management's rough estimate. Three plants (Chakan, Manesar, Sanand) and about 2,000 people including contract workers.

segments.name: Bosch Ltd - power solutions and aftermarket
segments.commentary: Retains powertrain/propulsion and mobility aftermarket. Management said the portfolios are complementary with no overlap. Bosch Automotive Electronics (captive contract manufacturer, low margin, high capex) is excluded from this deal and is under review.

guidance_outlook: Synergies not counted in the business case; post-merger integration of about 6-12 months to follow closing.
Target to complete acquisition by end of Q1 FY27, subject to shareholder approval.
Management expects to hold margins steady for about 5 years and to fund all major OEM projects through their 2031 launches.
Capex for the target guided at about 1.5%-3.5% of net sales in the business case; no firm capex figure given.
Dividend distribution policy of 55%-85% of PAT reiterated.
capex_capacity: Target's main plant is in Chakan; a large plant in Jharkhand; Manesar is an assembly unit and Sanand a warehouse, with management saying the current capacity is near max in its current locations.
Expansion is mostly brownfield, using idle lines from the Bosch global network (second-hand, pre-run lines) for faster ramp-up.
Each e-axle line produces about 150,000 units; the e-axle market is small in India and the 50:50 JV with Tata Autocomp is intended to consolidate volumes.
Management says it will add capacity only against legislation or confirmed OEM programmes.
demand_pricing: Management said the order book is very full, with a project pipeline for 4-5 years, and that no orders have been lost so far.
Two-wheeler ABS: management says Bosch holds a very high, market-leading share; a below-125cc ABS mandate is still under consideration with no new update.
Margins expected to face some pressure from OEMs wanting customized solutions and from cost-down pressure in ABS for the 2-wheeler segment, but management expects to hold margins steady.
Management said it is the market leader in passenger car ABS/ESP and the most advanced ESP is 10th generation.
Localization is over 90% of child parts for some Bosch Ltd products, according to management.

qa_highlights.question: Why was RBIC chosen now, and why not Bosch Automotive Electronics (related-party exposure)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RBIC is powertrain-agnostic and margin-accretive from day one. The automotive electronics entity is a captive, low-margin, capex-heavy contract manufacturer and is excluded for now but under ongoing review.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue mix and synergies?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly one-third two-wheeler and the rest cars and commercial vehicles. No synergies counted in the business case; they will be reviewed in post-merger integration.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the margin jump (gross margin from ~34% to ~40%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited scale, localization of products and child parts, legislation-led volume, modular platforms, and idle lines transferred from the Bosch network, with stable quality and productivity.

qa_highlights.question: Why was a preferential issue of only about INR8.8 crore disclosed and not the acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: The company secretary said the announcement covered only the preferential issue and that the acquisition details were UPSI before the board meeting. The questioner challenged the disclosure, and management said it would improve governance practice.

qa_highlights.question: Cash, funding and balance sheet after deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash consideration is covered and both companies will be debt-free post-deal. The company did not disclose the target's H1 cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Order book at RBIC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the order book as very full, with a 4-5 year project pipeline and good market share in all categories.

risks_watch: Related-party transaction exposure is rising: Bosch Automotive Electronics supplies to both entities on a cost-plus transfer price basis, and royalty terms are described as 'very similar'.
Governance: questions were raised on the adequacy of the April 1, 2026 board-meeting intimation, and the company was asked to improve disclosure.
Shareholder approval through the voting window ending May 8, 2026, and completion targeted by end-Q1 FY27.
Management views on the 2-wheeler ABS mandate for sub-125cc bikes remain unconfirmed; the deal business case excludes unlegislated upside.
Margin pressure in ABS for 2-wheelers and from Chinese competitors; the transfer price and cost-based structure will need monitoring post-close.
RBIC cash flow and capex figures were not disclosed; the cash flow figures stated as of 9M FY26 are unconfirmed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on strategic rationale and margins, but evasive on segment splits, the target's H1 cash flow, capex figures and disclosure timing; several answers were deferred to post-closing site visits.
key_quotes: So, we are very positive that this will do well for Bosch Limited and thank you for your interest and good questions today.
We believe at Bosch Limited this is a great synergy of integrating this company.
We believe we will hold margins very steady for the next 5 years or so.
And we have a completely captive, the largest captive engineering center of any auto company in India, close to 22,000 people work in that company

adds.what: Brownfield expansion using idle second-hand pre-run lines from Bosch global network at RBIC (Chakan main plant; large Jharkhand plant referenced)

growth.why: Call was about the RBIC acquisition, not quarterly results; management was in silent period. Pro forma FY25 revenue rises about 22% to INR22,000 crore via acquisition (inorganic, not organic guidance), with ~5% pro forma EPS accretion and margins guided steady for ~5 years; order book described as very full with 4-5 year pipeline, but no specific new capacity numbers or timelines beyond brownfield
